summary: Stefano Zacchetti was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Ca' Foscari University of Venice under Alfredo Cadonna, later holding posts at Padua, Soka University, Ca' Foscari (~2005–2012), and Oxford (~2012–2020).

Stella Kramrisch was an Indologist and art historian/archaeologist. After studying at the University of Vienna (~1914–1919), she held academic posts at the University of Calcutta (~1923–1950) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1950–1972).

Sten Konow worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Richard Pischel, served as Government Epigraphist for India, and held professorships at the University of Oslo, University of Hamburg, and Visva-Bharati University.
Stephan Beyer specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1977).
Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1983) under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephanie Kaza worked in religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at Oberlin, Stanford, Starr King School for the Ministry, and UC Santa Cruz, she served as Professor of Environmental Studies at the University of Vermont (~1991–2015).
Stephanie Roemer is a scholar in the field of Tibetology. She completed her doctoral studies under supervisors Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison is an Indologist and linguist. She studied at Yale University (~1969–1977) and held academic posts at Harvard University (~1986–1989) and the University of California, Los Angeles (~2002).

Stephen Addiss specialized in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1973–1977) and held professorships at the University of Kansas (~1977–1992) and the University of Richmond (~1992–2013).
Stephen Batchelor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Rabten, and Kusan Sunim, and held a post at Songgwangsa (1981–1984).

Stephen C. Berkwitz specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Kelaniya and has held posts at Missouri State University, Ruhr University Bochum, and the University of Colombo.

Stephen F. Teiser works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University (PhD ~1981–1986), subsequently holding faculty posts at Middlebury College (~1986–1988) and Princeton University (~1988–).

Stephen G. Covell works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at Princeton University (~1995–2001) under Jacqueline I. Stone and took up a post at Western Michigan University (~2003).

Stephen H. West is a sinologist who studied at National Taiwan Normal University and the University of Michigan (~1967–1972). He held professorships at the University of California, Berkeley (~1986–2004) and Arizona State University (~2004–2019).

Stephen J. Laumakis is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under John Kronen, Ramdas Lamb, and George J. Tanabe, Jr., and serves as a professor of philosophy at the University of St. Thomas.

Stephen L. Jenkins specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University, supervised by Masatoshi Nagatomi and Charles Hallisey, and served as Professor of Religious Studies at California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt.

Stephen Prothero is a scholar of religious studies. He completed his education at Yale University, Jonathan Edwards College, and Harvard University (~1986–1990), later joining the faculty at Boston University (~1996).

Stephen R. Bokenkamp is a sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley (~1976–1986). He held posts at Indiana University (~1989–2007), the Australian National University (1999), and Arizona State University (~2007).
Stephen Suen is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2009).

Steve Odin is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He completed graduate study at Stony Brook University (~1975–1980) under David A. Dilworth and Edward S. Casey, later becoming Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaii (1982).
